- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.0), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3), model often overcorrects downward; avoid sharp drops; add 1–2% to forecast if recent price is falling.
- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon (especially days 1–5), especially after spikes; apply downward bias of 2–5% for first 5 days.
- After a price spike (e.g., >85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >85 for 2+ consecutive days, reduce by 1–3% per day until price stabilizes.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0) and history shows no strong trend, model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to catch momentum.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in the last 5 days of 30-day window; apply smoothing or decay factor (e.g., 0.85 multiplier) to recent days.
